title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Heading (α): 'Fully faithful functors on categories of motives, linked to Hodge theory.'

Setting. S is a regular, connected Q-scheme with a geometric point ξ: Spec C → S. Mot(S) is the category of (pure, homological) motives of smooth projective S-schemes, called 'motifs lisses sur S'. Pullback ξ*: Mot(S) → Mot(C) is faithful. Composing with the Hodge realization T_{B,H}: Mot(C) → Hodge(Q,C) and the forgetful functor to finite Q-vector spaces gives the Betti fibre functor (T_B)_ξ. This is the fibre functor whose automorphism group is the motivic Galois group of the surrounding notes. The question is how much extra structure on T_B must be added to make the realization fully faithful.

(1) 'Via Hodge'. Assume ξ factors through the generic point η of S, so k(η) ⊂ C. To a motive M associate the triple (T_DR(M_η), T_B(M_ξ), φ_M), where:
- T_DR(M_η) is algebraic de Rham cohomology over k(η), with its Hodge filtration F;
- T_B(M_ξ) is the Betti Q-lattice;
- φ_M: T_B ⊗_Q C ≅ T_DR ⊗_{k(η)} C is the comparison isomorphism.
The filtration is required to be 'admissible' on the complexified Betti space, i.e. together with its complex conjugate it defines a bigrading (a pure Hodge structure). The margin label reads 'réseau et vectoriel filtré' (lattice plus filtered vector space).

The target category consists of Q-Hodge structures with a k(η)-form of the underlying C-space compatible with F. A morphism is a Q-linear map whose complexification preserves the k(η)-structures and F. Grothendieck claims this functor is fully faithful, conjecturally, i.e. granting the ordinary Hodge conjecture.

Proof sketch, valid granting Hodge:
- Reduce to S = η: homological correspondences on the generic fibre extend by closure.
- A morphism in the target is a Hodge class in Hom(T_B M, T_B N) whose de Rham class is k-rational.
- By the Hodge conjecture it is the class of a cycle Z over C, defined over a finite extension of k inside C (after spreading out).
- Its Galois conjugates have the same k-rational de Rham class, hence the same Betti class, since the comparison is injective.
- Averaging the conjugates gives a cycle over k with the given class.

(1b) The same is claimed for the triple (T_Hdg(M), T_B(M_ξ), ψ_M). Here T_Hdg = ⊕ H^q(Ω^p) over k(η), viewed as bigraded ('réseau et vectoriel bigradué'). ψ_M: T_B ⊗ C ≅ T_Hdg ⊗ C is the canonical Hodge decomposition, identifying H^{p,q} with H^q(Ω^p) ⊗ C. The structure is thus a Hodge structure plus k-forms of the graded pieces only.

Left margin, uncertain reading: 'le foncteur mot. → v.f. est pl. fidèle si on laisse tomber la filtration de T_DR ?? i.e. pour bigr. de T_Hdg !?' This asks whether full faithfulness survives if the Hodge filtration is dropped, i.e. for bare de Rham–Betti triples, and similarly for the bigraded variant.

Role. This is the first of three candidate 'realization' descriptions of Mot(S), each meant to describe the motivic Galois group by a Tannakian full subcategory of linear-algebra data:
- Hodge, this page;
- ℓ-adic Galois representations via Tate, next page;
- de Rham with Gauss–Manin stratification plus Betti, next page.
errors: Full faithfulness is conjectural (it depends on the Hodge conjecture, as Grothendieck says), not a theorem.

For the passage from S to η one needs that homological correspondences over η extend to S, and that homological equivalence is compatible. This holds for smooth projective S-schemes over a regular base via closures, but it is left implicit.

Variant (1b) is stated without argument and the margin shows doubt ('!?'). It is in fact correct granting Hodge. A Hodge class whose (p,p) image in H^p(Ω^p) is k-rational: write it as cl(Z), Z defined over L ⊃ k. For σ ∈ Gal(L/k), cl(Z) − cl(σZ) is a rational class of type (p,p) lying in F^{p+1}, hence zero. So the de Rham class is k-rational and one reduces to (1a).

The margin question about dropping the filtration has a different answer depending on k. For k(η) = C, or k of large transcendence degree, the bare triple carries too little information; for k = C the Hom spaces become all of Hom_Q. For k = Q̄ it is equivalent to (a form of) the Grothendieck period conjecture, not the Hodge conjecture.

ideas.what: Betti fibre functor at a geometric point of a regular base; faithfulness of ξ* on smooth motives over S
ideas.modern_name: Betti fibre functor / Tannakian motivic Galois group of motives over a base
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (motivic Galois group), Saavedra Rivano 1972, Deligne–Milne 1982
ideas.where_published: Only via Saavedra's thesis and Grothendieck's oral or letter communications; unsure of any Grothendieck-authored text

ideas.what: Realization of motives over k ⊂ C as (filtered de Rham k-space, Betti Q-lattice, comparison iso) with the filtration giving a Hodge structure; full faithfulness from the Hodge conjecture
ideas.modern_name: Category of (Hodge–de Rham) realizations / systems of realizations; full faithfulness of the realization functor; absolute Hodge philosophy
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge cycles on abelian varieties, 1982; 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points', 1989), Jannsen 1990 (mixed realizations)
ideas.where_published: Related remarks in 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966) and 'Standard conjectures' (1969); this exact formulation not known to me in print

ideas.what: Variant with Hodge cohomology ⊕H^q(Ω^p) over k, bigraded, plus Betti lattice via the Hodge decomposition, also claimed fully faithful
ideas.modern_name: Hodge structure with k-rational structure on graded pieces (k-forms of H^{p,q}); no standard name

ideas.what: Margin query: full faithfulness for bare de Rham–Betti triples (filtration dropped)
ideas.modern_name: de Rham–Betti structures; full faithfulness of Mot(Q̄) → DRB, equivalent to (a form of) the Grothendieck period conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (period conjecture, footnote in 1966 de Rham paper); developed by André (2004), Bost–Charles (2016)
ideas.where_published: Period conjecture alluded to in 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966); full-faithfulness phrasing is later (André, Bost–Charles)

missed.claim: As early as 1965, explicitly within the motivic Galois group programme, Grothendieck formulates the 'Hodge realization with de Rham k-structure' as a fully faithful functor out of motives over a regular base, conditional on the Hodge conjecture. Historians usually attribute this circle of ideas to Deligne's 1982 absolute Hodge and realization framework.
missed.quote: Le foncteur M ↦ ainsi obtenu est pleinement fidèle (moyennant conj. de Hodge simple)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority rather than new mathematics: the realization-category approach to motives was present in Grothendieck's original Tannakian programme.

missed.claim: Variant (b) replaces filtered de Rham cohomology by k-forms on the Hodge graded pieces H^q(Ω^p) only. It is asserted with a doubtful '!?' and not proved. It is correct granting the Hodge conjecture, by a short Galois-averaging argument plus F^{p+1} ∩ (p,p) = 0. Such a 'graded Hodge–de Rham' realization category is not a standard object in the literature.
missed.quote: Même résultat si on considère {T_Hdg(M), T_B(M_ξ), ψ_M} T_Hdg(M) étant considéré comme bigradué
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a weaker linear-algebra datum that still (conjecturally) pins down morphisms of motives. This is mildly relevant to discussions of de Rham–Betti and Hodge–Betti structures and to which period data detect cycles.

missed.claim: If the margin reading is right, Grothendieck asks whether full faithfulness persists after dropping the Hodge filtration, i.e. for bare (T_DR, T_B, φ) triples. This is exactly the de Rham–Betti full-faithfulness question that later became a reformulation of his period conjecture (André; Bost–Charles). It appears here in 1965, near-contemporaneous with the 1966 footnote.
missed.quote: le foncteur mot. → v.f. est pl. fidèle si on laisse tomber [?] la filtration de T_DR ?? i.e. pour bigr. de T_Hdg !?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Possibly the earliest written trace linking the period conjecture to full faithfulness of a realization functor. The reading of the margin is uncertain.

deep.surprise_reason: The main content (Hodge plus de Rham realization fully faithful under the Hodge conjecture) is known through Deligne and Jannsen, though seeing it in Grothendieck's 1965 motivic Galois notes is a nice priority detail. The bigraded-Hodge-cohomology variant and the margin query about dropping the filtration (a precursor of the de Rham–Betti period-conjecture formulation) are small but genuinely unrecorded details. Nothing here is a deep unknown result.
transcription_corrections: 'S-noyau[?] ξ localisé au pt générique η de S' should read '(1) Supposons ξ localisé au pt générique de S' ('Supposons').
'filtration admissible[?] des contraintes[?] de T_B(M_ξ)' is likely 'filtration admissible du complexifié de T_B(M_ξ)', i.e. of T_B ⊗ C.
'(conjecturalement conj. de Hodge simple)' is more likely '(moyennant conj. de Hodge simple)'.
Left margin: 'si on connaît[?] la filtration' is plausibly 'si on laisse tomber la filtration de T_DR ??', which fits the logic of the question marks.
In the formula for ψ_M the tensor is T_B(M_ξ) ⊗_Q C; the handwritten subscript under the first ⊗ looks like 'DR' but is a slip or overwrite.
'(a)' next to 'À tout' is a circled 'a' marker paired with '(b)' later, labelling variants (a) and (b).
